def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear:
## Definition

Let $m,n$ be nonnegative integers, $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, and $c\in\mathbb R^n$. The standard-form minimization linear program with data $(A,b,c)$ is
$$\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}.$$
Its feasible set is $P(A,b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\}$, and a feasible $x$ is optimal if $c^{\mathsf T}x\le c^{\mathsf T}z$ for every $z\in P(A,b)$. The notation $x\ge0$ is componentwise. The revised-simplex basis algorithms on this page require a full-row-rank matrix, meaning $\operatorname{rank}(A)=m$; a rank-deficient raw system must first be reduced by exact row operations, with inconsistent rows reported as infeasible. For $m=0$, the empty system has its usual zero-dimensional interpretation.

A vector $q\in\mathbb R^m$ satisfying $A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0$ and $b^{\mathsf T}q<0$ is called a **Farkas infeasibility certificate** for this sign convention. Indeed, any feasible $x\ge0$ would give $b^{\mathsf T}q=x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0$.

A vector $q\in\mathbb R^m$ satisfying $A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0$ and $b^{\mathsf T}q<0$ is called a **Farkas infeasibility certificate** for this sign convention. Indeed, any feasible $x\ge0$ would give $b^{\mathsf T}q=x^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0$.
def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary:
## Definition

Use the standard-form problem of [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]]. Assume $A$ has full row rank $m$. An ordered basis is a list $B=(B_1,\ldots,B_m)$ of distinct column indices for which the square matrix $A_B=[a_{B_1}\ \cdots\ a_{B_m}]$ is invertible. Write $N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}$ and $c_B=(c_{B_1},\ldots,c_{B_m})^{\mathsf T}$. The basic vector $x(B)$ is defined by $x_B(B)=A_B^{-1}b$ and $x_j(B)=0$ for $j\in N$; the basis is primal feasible, and $x(B)$ is a basic feasible solution, exactly when $A_B^{-1}b\ge0$.

The basis multiplier is $y(B)=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B$. For every column $j$, its reduced cost is $\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y(B)$. In particular, $\bar c_{B_i}=0$ for each basic index. The basis is dual feasible when $\bar c_j\ge0$ for every $j\in N$. When $m=0$, take the empty basis and the empty multiplier; these formulas remain meaningful.

A primal-feasible basis is **degenerate** if some basic coordinate is zero. A simplex pivot is **degenerate** if its ratio-test step length is zero.
alg-revised-simplex-residual-audit:
## Definition

Input a standard-form problem as in [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]], whose stored matrix, right-hand side, and cost entries are finite binary floating-point values, together with finite stored candidate vectors $\hat x\in\mathbb R^n$ and $\hat y\in\mathbb R^m$. A finite binary value is interpreted as its exact dyadic rational (an integer times an integer power of $2$). If a dimension is wrong or any value is NaN or infinite, return `invalid-input`. Otherwise use exact integer/rational arithmetic to compute $r_p=A\hat x-b$, $r_d=c-A^{\mathsf T}\hat y$, $g=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x-b^{\mathsf T}\hat y$, $\rho_p=\|r_p\|_\infty$, and $\rho_d=\|r_d\|_\infty$, where $\|z\|_\infty=\max_i|z_i|$ and the empty-vector value is zero. Return these exact values and $|g|$ as the exact primal-dual objective difference for the stored data. Return `verified-optimal-for-stored-data` exactly when $\hat x\ge0$, $r_p=0$, $r_d\ge0$, and $g=0$. In every other finite-input case return `candidate-only` with the residuals and gap; a nonzero or small residual is never rounded to zero and does not certify infeasibility.

The exact arithmetic is a verification procedure for a candidate produced by a floating-point solver; it does not define a basis factorization or bound uncertainty in data before they were stored. If a statement about pre-rounded data is required, separate certified input intervals must be supplied and propagated. The procedure makes no operation-count or runtime claim.
lem-revised-simplex-basic-feasible-extre:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ have full row rank and let $P(A,b)$ be the feasible set of [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]]. For a feasible $x$, define its support by $S(x)=\{j:x_j>0\}$. A set $C$ is **convex** if $tu+(1-t)v\in C$ for all $u,v\in C$ and $0<t<1$. A point $x\in C$ is an **extreme point** if every representation $x=tu+(1-t)v$ with $u,v\in C$ and $0<t<1$ forces $u=v=x$. Then $x$ is an extreme point of $P(A,b)$ if and only if the columns $\{a_j:j\in S(x)\}$ are linearly independent. This is equivalent to $x$ being a basic feasible solution for [[def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary]]. In particular, every nonempty $P(A,b)$ has a basic feasible solution. The statement includes $m=0$ using the empty-basis convention.
thm-revised-simplex-primal-pivot-objecti:
## Statement

Let $B$ be a primal-feasible basis for the standard-form problem of [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]] and [[def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary]], and let $j$ be a nonbasic index with reduced cost $\bar c_j<0$. Put $d=A_B^{-1}a_j$. If $d_i\le0$ for every basic row $i$, then $r_j=1$, $r_B=-d$, and $r_k=0$ for the other nonbasic indices define a feasible ray with $Ar=0$ and $c^{\mathsf T}r=\bar c_j<0$; the LP is unbounded below. If some $d_i>0$, the step $\theta=\min_{d_i>0}(x_{B_i}/d_i)$ is finite and nonnegative, every minimizing row gives a valid pivot, the new basic vector is feasible, and the objective change is $\theta\bar c_j\le0$, strictly negative exactly when $\theta>0$. Finally, if all nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative at a primal-feasible basis, its basic vector is optimal.
alg-revised-primal-simplex-bland-rule:
## Definition

Input the exact standard-form data of [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]] with full-row-rank $A$ and a primal-feasible basis $B$ as in [[def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary]]. Use exact arithmetic. At each iteration compute $x_B=A_B^{-1}b$, $y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B$, and all nonbasic reduced costs $\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y$.

1. If every nonbasic $\bar c_j\ge0$, return `optimal` with $x(B)$ and $y$.
2. Otherwise choose the least index $j\notin B$ with $\bar c_j<0$ and solve $A_Bd=a_j$.
3. If no component $d_i$ is positive, return `unbounded` with the ray whose $j$th component is $1$, whose basic components are $-d$, and whose other nonbasic components are $0$.
4. Otherwise compute $\theta=\min_{d_i>0}x_{B_i}/d_i$. Among minimizing rows, leave the basic variable of least index. Replace its basis column by $a_j$ and repeat.

The algorithm assumes an exact initial feasible basis. It makes no iteration bound polynomial in $m$ or $n$.
alg-revised-dual-simplex-with-finite-bud:
## Definition

Input the exact standard-form data and a basis $B$ for which every nonbasic reduced cost is nonnegative, as in [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]] and [[def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary]]. Also input a nonnegative integer pivot budget $K$. Set $k=0$ and repeat:

1. Compute $x_B=A_B^{-1}b$ and $y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B$. If $x_B\ge0$, return `optimal` with the primal basic vector and $y$.
2. Otherwise choose the least-index basic variable $B_i$ with $x_{B_i}<0$. For each nonbasic $j$ compute $d_{ij}=(A_B^{-1}a_j)_i$. If no $d_{ij}<0$, return `infeasible` with $q=A_B^{-\mathsf T}e_i$.
3. If $k=K$, return `pivot-budget-exhausted` with the current basis and its dual-feasible multiplier.
4. Among $j$ with $d_{ij}<0$, choose one minimizing $\bar c_j/(-d_{ij})$, with least variable index among ties. Replace $B_i$ by $j$, set $k\leftarrow k+1$, and repeat.

The procedure preserves dual feasibility, but the budget-exhausted status is inconclusive. No finite-success or anti-cycling claim is part of this definition.
prop-revised-simplex-sparse-pricing-oper:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be represented by a valid CSR record with row pointers $r$, column indices $c_t$, values $v_t$, and $s$ stored entries, under [[def-csr-matrix-with-stored-entry-semantics]]. For each $0\le t<s$, let $i(t)$ be the unique row satisfying $r_{i(t)}\le t<r_{i(t)+1}$. For a cost vector $c\in\mathbb R^n$ and given $y\in\mathbb R^m$, initialize $w\in\mathbb R^n$ to zero and, for $t=0,\ldots,s-1$, update
$$w_{c_t}\leftarrow w_{c_t}+v_ty_{i(t)}.$$
In exact real arithmetic the resulting vector is $A^{\mathsf T}y$. This loop uses exactly $s$ multiplications and $s$ additions, followed by $n$ zero initializations; forming $c-w$ uses $n$ subtractions and gives the reduced-cost vector of [[def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary]] when $y=y(B)$. Every stored entry is counted, including repeated column indices and explicitly stored zeros. The claim is an arithmetic-operation count; it gives no runtime, bandwidth, or factorization bound.
thm-revised-simplex-primal-dual-residual:
## Statement

For a standard-form problem and finite candidate vectors $x,y$, let $r_p=Ax-b$, $r_d=c-A^{\mathsf T}y$, and $g=c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y$, as computed exactly by [[alg-revised-simplex-residual-audit]]. Then
$$g=x^{\mathsf T}r_d+y^{\mathsf T}r_p,$$
and consequently
$$|g|\le \|x\|_1\|r_d\|_\infty+\|y\|_1\|r_p\|_\infty.$$
Here $\|z\|_1=\sum_i|z_i|$ and $\|z\|_\infty=\max_i|z_i|$, with both norms equal to zero on the empty vector. This bounds the primal-dual objective difference for the stored data; when either vector is infeasible it does not bound distance to an optimal value. If $Ax=b$, $x\ge0$, $c-A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0$, and $g=0$, then $x$ is optimal.
thm-revised-simplex-bland-rule-finite-te:
## Statement

For exact arithmetic and a finite standard-form LP with full-row-rank $A$, the primal algorithm of [[alg-revised-primal-simplex-bland-rule]], started from any primal-feasible basis, terminates after finitely many pivots at an optimal basis or returns a feasible ray of strictly negative cost. If the feasible set is nonempty and the objective is bounded below, an optimal basis exists and is returned. The number of pivots is at most the number of possible bases, hence at most $\binom{n}{m}$; this is a finiteness bound, not a polynomial-time claim. Every pivot may be degenerate, so the objective need not decrease strictly at each step.
thm-revised-dual-simplex-invariant-and-f:
## Statement

Let $B$ be a basis of the minimization problem for which all nonbasic reduced costs are nonnegative. At an iteration of [[alg-revised-dual-simplex-with-finite-budget]], a pivot chosen from a row $i$ with $x_{B_i}<0$ and a column $j$ with $d_{ij}=(A_B^{-1}a_j)_i<0$ minimizing $\bar c_j/(-d_{ij})$ preserves dual feasibility. If there is no nonbasic $j$ with $d_{ij}<0$, then $q=A_B^{-\mathsf T}e_i$ satisfies $A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0$ and $b^{\mathsf T}q<0$, so $q$ is a Farkas infeasibility certificate as defined in [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]] and the primal problem is infeasible. If the current basis is both primal and dual feasible, it is optimal. A finite pivot-budget exhaustion is inconclusive and does not assert infeasibility or convergence.
alg-revised-simplex-phase-one:
## Definition

Input any exact equality system $Ax=b$ with $x\ge0$, including a rank-deficient raw system. Let $D$ be diagonal with $D_{ii}=-1$ when $b_i<0$ and $D_{ii}=1$ otherwise; set $\widetilde A=DA$ and $\widetilde b=Db\ge0$. Add artificial variables $u\in\mathbb R^m$ and solve the Phase I problem $\min\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u$ subject to $\widetilde A x+u=\widetilde b$, $x,u\ge0$, starting at $x=0,u=\widetilde b$ with artificial basis $I_m$. Use the exact primal algorithm of [[alg-revised-primal-simplex-bland-rule]] and its finite-termination result [[thm-revised-simplex-bland-rule-finite-termination]].

At a terminal optimum, if $\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u>0$, return `infeasible` and the basis multiplier $y$ for the Phase I objective. If the optimum is zero, set every artificial variable to zero and remove artificial basic variables as follows. For a zero-valued artificial basic variable, inspect its row in $B^{-1}\widetilde A$. If some original nonbasic column has a nonzero coefficient there, pivot the least-index such column into the basis; the pivot may have either sign because the leaving basic value is zero. If no such coefficient exists, and the transformed right-hand-side entry is zero, delete that redundant equation and its zero artificial basic variable. Repeat until all remaining basic columns are original; return the row-reduced equivalent system and its original feasible basis. A zero row with nonzero transformed right-hand side returns `inconsistent-row`. All tests are exact; a finite-precision near-zero objective is not treated as zero.
thm-revised-simplex-phase-one-extraction:
## Statement

For any exact system $Ax=b$, $x\ge0$, the Phase I procedure of [[alg-revised-simplex-phase-one]] terminates. Its minimum artificial-variable sum is zero if and only if the original system is feasible. If the minimum is positive, its returned vector yields a Farkas infeasibility certificate, as defined in [[def-revised-simplex-standard-form-linear-program]], with $A^{\mathsf T}q\ge0$ and $b^{\mathsf T}q<0$. If the minimum is zero, the extraction procedure returns an equivalent full-row-rank reduced system with a basic feasible solution using only original columns; zero-valued artificial basic variables are either pivoted out or their redundant equations are removed.
alg-revised-simplex-qr-basis-recompute-a:
## Definition

Input finite stored binary data for the standard-form LP of [[def-revised-simplex-basis-dictionary]], with full-row-rank $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, a valid ordered basis $B$, and a nonnegative integer budget $K$ of basis evaluations. Stored values represent their exact dyadic rationals. Invalid dimensions, nonfinite inputs or repeated/out-of-range basis indices return `invalid-input`. Nonsingularity of $C=A_B$ must be established as part of an admitted basis input; a numerical rank threshold is not such an establishment. A basis whose validity is unavailable returns `basis-validity-inconclusive`.

A caller may request a primal or dual simplex transition after an audit, or only an audit. It may supply a finite sequence of valid transitions from the existing exact OPT13 methods. A transition record identifies the leaving position and entering nonbasic index and establishes the exact primal or dual sign/ratio hypotheses for that transition and nonsingularity of its new basis. Exact OPT13 pivot checks suffice. Certified enclosures with a justified conditioning bound may also suffice, but this procedure does not manufacture such a bound or infer a sign from a small residual. A floating proposal lacking an established transition returns `pivot-inconclusive`, without changing the basis. Thus this interface composes both exact primal/dual drivers and guarded numerical proposals; it does not redefine their pivot rules.

For $m\ge1$, use the operationwise arithmetic of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with $0<u<1$, $mu<1$, $(m+3)u<1$, and $\gamma_{m+3}<1/8$. All nonzero exact intermediates must be normal. Norms and certificate expressions below are evaluated exactly or by certified upward bounds; failure to obtain a finite valid bound is a numerical failure. Process the following loop:

1. If $K$ basis evaluations have been attempted, return `budget-exhausted` with the last completed audit, if any. Count this attempt before starting a factorization.
2. Recompute QR of $C=A_B$ and of $C^{\mathsf T}$ from their current original stored entries, by the canonical successive calls to [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] used in [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]]. Apply stored reflectors to right-hand sides by the analyzed rounded rank-one updates and use successful rounded triangular substitution. Compute $\widehat x_B$ from $Cz=b$, $\widehat y$ from $C^{\mathsf T}z=c_B$, and $\widehat d_j$ from $Cz=a_j$ for the finitely many requested nonbasic columns. Reuse the current $C$ factorization for its separate right-hand sides. Never substitute a rounded dense orthogonal product for the exact orthogonal representative in the proof. After every admitted basis replacement discard both factorizations and recompute; no rank-one factorization-update implementation is claimed.
3. Independently certify each returned solve for its actual current matrix $D=C$ or $C^{\mathsf T}$ and right-hand side $r$. Compute $\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(D\widehat z)$ and $\widehat w=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-r)$ by the sequential products/subtraction of [[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]]. Put
$$g_m=\frac{1+6u}{1-(m-1)u}-1,\qquad W=g_m\|D\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+\|r\|_2).$$
With the local coefficient $\kappa_m$ of [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]], put
$$\beta=(1+\kappa_m)^m-1,\qquad \beta_D=\beta+\gamma_{m+3}(1+\beta),$$
and report the valid upper bound
$$\eta(D,r,\widehat z)=\min\{\|\widehat w\|_2+W,\ \beta_D\|D\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+\beta\|r\|_2\}.$$
A finite concrete certificate option uses exact rational arithmetic on the stored dyadic entries and a rational upper bound for $u$ satisfying all displayed admissibility inequalities. Use $\|v\|_2\le\sum_i|v_i|$ and $\|D\|_F\le\sum_{i,j}|D_{ij}|$ as rational upper bounds for every norm in the two nonnegative expressions. For the local coefficient, substitute $\bar e_m=(1+u)^{m+3}-1$ for $e_m=(1+u)^{m/2+3}-1$ in the source formula: put $\bar d_m=\bar e_m+u(2+\bar e_m)$, $a_m=(1+u)/(1-u)^m-1$, $g_m^{\rm QR}=mu/(1-mu)$, $c_m=2((1+a_m)(1+u)^2(1+g_m^{\rm QR})-1)$, and $\bar\kappa_m=\max\{\bar e_m+8\bar d_m,(1+u)c_m+3u\}$. These are rational upper bounds because $m+3\ge m/2+3$ and all constituent nonnegative formulas increase in their arguments. Then $\bar\beta=(1+\bar\kappa_m)^m-1$ and $\bar\beta_D=\bar\beta+\gamma_{m+3}(1+\bar\beta)$ are rational upper bounds for the QR coefficients. Compute both candidate bounds by finite exact rational sums/products/powers and take their minimum as the returned $\eta$. This implements the certificate without a norm oracle; other finite certified upper-bound procedures are allowed. Any factorization, substitution, dot, subtraction, range or certificate failure returns `numerical-failure`, with its stage and the last completed audit; it returns no certificate for the failed solve.
4. Embed $\widehat x_B$ in $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n$ with zero nonbasic entries, and call [[alg-revised-simplex-residual-audit]] on these actual stored $\widehat x,\widehat y$. Retain its exact $r_p=A\widehat x-b$, $r_d=c-A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y$, objective difference $g$, and audit status together with all solve residual bounds. `basis-solves-residual-certified` means only that the returned bounds certify those linear equations; any requested thresholds must also be checked before declaring them met. `verified-optimal-for-stored-data` is issued only by the exact audit's primal/sign/zero-gap checks. Other completed candidates remain `candidate-only`; small residuals or a failed/ambiguous pivot never certify infeasibility.
5. Return if audit-only mode or the caller has no further transition. Otherwise accept only an established transition of the declared type. An unresolved sign, leaving-ratio comparison, tie or basis validity returns `pivot-inconclusive` or `basis-validity-inconclusive`, retaining the last completed audit and current basis. After an admitted replacement, continue at step1 with the new basis. Exact driver invariants remain those of the existing driver, not consequences of successful floating solves.

For $m=0$, skip QR and substitution: the basis, multiplier and direction arrays are empty and their basis-equation residuals are zero. Evaluate the existing exact audit with $\widehat x=0$; no basis replacement is possible. The budget and invalid-input branches remain in force.
thm-revised-simplex-qr-basis-residual-st:
## Statement

For admitted inputs of [[alg-revised-simplex-qr-basis-recompute-and-audit]], the procedure terminates after at most $K$ basis-evaluation attempts with its defined output or failure status. Each completed solve certificate satisfies
$$\|D\widehat z-r\|_2\le\eta(D,r,\widehat z)$$
for its actual current $D=A_B$ or $A_B^{\mathsf T}$ and right-hand side. If $z_*=D^{-1}r$ denotes the exact solution, then also $\|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le\|D^{-1}\|_2\eta(D,r,\widehat z)$. This inequality does not compute or bound the inverse norm. In particular, its returned $\widehat x_B,\widehat y,\widehat d_j$ have the respective certified primal-basis, multiplier and direction residuals. Its exact stored-data audit obeys
$$g=\widehat x^{\mathsf T}r_d+\widehat y^{\mathsf T}r_p,\qquad |g|\le\|\widehat x\|_1\|r_d\|_\infty+\|\widehat y\|_1\|r_p\|_\infty.$$
Only the exact audit's feasibility, dual-sign and zero-gap checks issue `verified-optimal-for-stored-data`. Every unestablished transition or unresolved sign/ratio comparison stops without changing the basis. The theorem grants neither forward accuracy without conditioning nor correctness of unvalidated floating pivot choices, an infeasibility certificate from near-zero data, or numerical termination at an optimum.
